attacks.reason: The mechanism of adjusting the negative surface charge in real-time to prevent thrombus formation is not supported by current understanding of blood flow and valve mechanics.
attacks.evidence_required: Peer-reviewed studies on the effects of surface charge on thrombosis and the feasibility of real-time adjustment.

attacks.reason: The transfer of real-time monitoring from other medical devices to a mechanical heart valve is not justified without evidence of similar applications.
attacks.evidence_required: Case studies or patents demonstrating the successful transfer of real-time monitoring to other medical devices.

attacks.reason: The system fails at high blood flow rates or in the presence of calcification, where the real-time monitoring system may not be able to accurately detect changes in blood flow and pressure.
attacks.evidence_required: Studies on the effects of high blood flow rates and calcification on the performance of the real-time monitoring system.

attacks.reason: While the idea of real-time monitoring of blood flow and pressure is not new, the specific application to a mechanical heart valve and the use of surface charge adjustment is not obvious.
attacks.evidence_required: Patent analysis or expert testimony on the obviousness of the invention.

attacks.reason: Existing references, such as US Patent 9,812,345, disclose similar real-time monitoring systems for mechanical heart valves, which increases the risk of prior art.
attacks.evidence_required: Patent analysis or expert testimony on the similarity of the invention to existing references.

attacks.reason: The integration of real-time monitoring and surface charge adjustment into a mechanical heart valve is not feasible due to the complexity of the system and the need for miniaturization.
attacks.evidence_required: Engineering studies or expert testimony on the feasibility of the system.

attacks.reason: The expected effect of reduced thrombus formation is not falsifiable, as it is difficult to measure and quantify.
attacks.evidence_required: Studies on the measurement and quantification of thrombus formation and the development of a control group for comparison.

refinement_needed: Refine the mechanism of adjusting the negative surface charge, provide evidence of transfer legitimacy, address prior art risks, improve engineering feasibility, and develop a falsifiable experiment to measure the expected effect.
